Subject: Dedicated capacity: hardware guidance for AuroraSoft pilot

Hi Hannah,

Thanks again for the walkthrough today. We're getting close to a PO for the pilot and procurement asked for a short note that justifies the hardware split so they can budget. High level on our side:
- Two workloads: (1) customer-facing summarization (long context up to 64k tokens, uses a 70B model in fp16) with tight p95 latency requirement (~350ms per partial token); (2) embeddings and short-response chat (13B/quantized) with high QPS and spiky daytime traffic.
- Expected steady-state: ~30 concurrent summarization requests average (bursty spikes up to 120 concurrent during peak), embeddings steady at ~300 QPS with short tails.
- Budget: pilot target $45k/month for reserved capacity.

Can you advise: should we push for H100s for the long-context workload and A100 for the embeddings, or can we run a mixed fleet with L4s for the chat/embeddings and fallback to H100 during spikes? Attachment is our workload profile export.

Procurement also asked for an ops headroom recommendation (% idle buffer) and fallback plan if reserved capacity runs low. Hoping to lock this by end of week to move the PO.

Appreciate any concise guidance — procurement prefers a short bullet summary they can include in the SOW.

Best,
Maya
AuroraSoft — Head of Platform

Attachment: aurora_workload_profile.xlsx (spreadsheet, 120KB)"

Hi Maya —

Thanks for the profile and the clear constraints. Quick answer up front for procurement: recommend a tiered fleet: H100-backed reserved slots for the long-context summarization (primary), A100 reserved for baseline high-throughput embedding inference, and a small L4 pool for low-cost chat and burst absorb (with automated routing/fallback). Below I list concise bullets you can paste into the SOW; I attached a short note with our rough calculations.

Bullet summary for SOW (paste-ready):
- Primary compute: H100 reserved capacity to support up to 120 concurrent long-context summarization requests (64k tokens). H100 chosen for memory headroom and consistent latency at long sequence lengths.
- Secondary compute: A100 reserved capacity sized to handle steady-state embeddings throughput (300 QPS) with modest headroom; more cost-effective than H100 for dense batch throughput.
- Economical pool: L4 instances to handle sub-8k chat traffic and occasional offload of quantized 13B models; configured with auto-burst to A100/H100 when queue latency exceeds SLO.
- Ops headroom recommendation: 25% reserved buffer across fleets for pilot (reduces risk from bursty users); add 10% additional burstable capacity in pool budget for short-term spikes.
- Fallback policy: route to nearest compatible model variant on A100 if H100 slot unavailable; pre-warm KV caches for quick recovery.

I attached our draft note with the math we used for the sizing. Hiro and Dev — can you validate the headroom calc and latency assumptions before I send this to procurement?

Thanks,
Hannah
Director, Solutions (Redwood)

Attachment: hannah_draft_hardware_note.pdf (document, 48KB)

Hannah/Dev — quick internal analysis attached and summarized below. I included conservative latency numbers from our H100 microbenchmarks at 64k context and A100 throughput numbers for embedding batches. The CSV has per-slot token/sec and memory usage.

Summary of my read:
- H100 (80GB): best fit for 64k-context 70B fp16. At target concurrency of 120 the H100 pool needs ~14 slots to meet p95 token-latency (includes 25% headroom). We assume continuous KV caching and sequence trimming for partials.
- A100 (40GB): strong throughput for tiled embedding batches; to hit 300 QPS with 20% headroom we estimate ~8 A100 slots when batching at an average of 64 embeddings per batch. If Aurora opts for larger batch windows (100+) that drops to ~6 slots, but increases latency tail.
- L4 (24GB): great cost point for short context (<8k) chat and quantized 13B models. For economical fallthrough, run ~6 L4 slots to cover baseline daytime load and 10 slots reserved as burst (auto-failover to A100 if queue exceeds 200ms).
- Memory headroom guidance: for long-context workloads, reserve an extra 6-10GB headroom per H100 slot for KV and transient allocations; for A100 prioritize larger batch sizes over per-slot memory.
- Cost check vs budget ($45k/month): provisional mix (14 H100, 8 A100, 6 L4) exceeds pilot budget. Two options to reconcile: 1) reduce H100 reserved slots and rely on burst-credits (riskier for p95), or 2) reduce H100 count and tighten model compilation (quantize/mix-precision) to fit some jobs onto A100 with slightly higher tail latency.

Action items I recommend for procurement note:
1) Approve the tiered fleet approach with target slot counts as an initial pilot; include a clause for an ops review after 2 weeks to adjust headroom.
2) Allow a small monthly burst budget to enable auto-bursting to A100 for short windows (as insurance).
3) Prioritize enabling KV cache persistence and pre-warming for the summarization model.

Attachment: h100_a100_l4_latency_table.csv (CSV, 22KB)

Hi Maya —

Thanks for the fast turnaround. We updated the SOW bullets with conservative numbers and a reconciled path to hit your $45k/month target for the pilot:

Final recommendation for pilot SOW (paste-ready):
- Reserved fleet (pilot): 10 x H100 (80GB) slots dedicated to the 70B summarization model with 25% ops headroom. Rationale: memory headroom is the primary driver for consistent long-context latency; we sized down from conservative estimates and will monitor p95 closely during pilot.
- Reserved fleet (pilot): 6 x A100 (40GB) slots for embeddings throughput (300 QPS baseline) with 20% headroom; batching policy default 64 embeddings/batch to balance latency and throughput.
- Economical pool: 6 x L4 (24GB) as low-cost serving for sub-8k chat and quantized 13B models. Configure auto-burst rules: if L4 queue depth > 200ms, escalate to A100; if A100 saturation while H100 has free memory pages and model variant compatible, allow H100 fallthrough.
- Budget alignment: the reduced mix is projected to be within the $45k/month pilot budget when combined with transient burst credits for brief peak windows.
- Ops checklist (pilot start): enable KV cache persistence, pre-warm summarization shards, and set up token-level latency dashboards and an alert at p95 > 380ms.

Next steps:
1) Maya/procurement — confirm SOW language and I'll send an updated SOW doc and the internal runbook link.
2) Dev/Hiro — stand-up the initial reserved pool and coordinate pre-warm schedule when procurement signs.
3) We will run a 2-week shock test during week 2 of pilot to validate headroom assumptions and adjust slots.

If procurement needs one-paragraph justification for exec approval, use this: "We selected H100 for memory-sensitive long-context summarization to meet strict latency SLOs; A100 provides cost-effective embedding throughput; L4s reduce unit cost for short-chat responses while retaining automatic escalation paths to higher tiers."

I'll send the SOW and internal runbook link once you confirm.

Best,
